'''Shinagadani Kofun Group''' (磯長谷古墳群) is a group of [[Kofun|Kofuns]] centered around {{ill|Japanese imperial tombs|en|Japanese imperial tombs|qid=Q17218816|lt=Japanese imperial tombs}} located in {{ill|Taishi, Osaka|en|Taishi, Osaka|qid=Q1347173|lt=Taishi, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}.
== Overview ==
The Shinagadani Kofun Group comprises approximately 30 Kofuns, including four mausoleums designated as [[Japanese imperial tombs|imperial tombs]] by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} ({{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|敏達天皇陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}, {{ill|Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|ja|春日向山古墳|4=de|5=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|6=fr|7=Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|lt_ja=用明天皇陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Mukaiyama Kofun|qq=}}, {{ill|Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|ja|山田高塚古墳|推古天皇陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}}, and {{ill|Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|ja|山田上ノ山古墳|孝徳天皇陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Uenoyama Kofun|qq=}}), along with the {{ill|Eifuku-ji North Kofun|ja|叡福寺北古墳|4=fr|5=Eifukuji Kita Kofun|lt_ja=聖徳太子墓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eifuku-ji North Kofun|qq=}}. These Kofuns date to the late {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} to the early {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|qid=Q210688|lt=Asuka period}}, between the mid-6th and early 7th centuries. Notably, the {{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|敏達天皇陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} is the only {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} within this group.
The five main tumuli (four Imperial mausolea and Prince Shōtoku's tomb) are collectively referred to as the "'''Umebachi Mausoleums'''" (梅鉢御陵), likened to the petals of a plum blossom. The area, located on the broad valley slopes of {{ill|Futakami Mountain|ja|二上山|2=ja|3=二上山|lt=Mount Futakami (or Nijo)|comment=Kanji are ambiguous between the two pronounciations|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Nijō|13=User:Immanuelle/Futakami Mountain|qq=}}, is also known as the "'''Valley of Royal Tombs'''." (王陵の谷).

=== Other Kofuns ===
Significant Kofuns in the area include:
; {{ill|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|en|Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)|qid=Q11371443|lt=Futagozuka Kofun (Osaka)}}
: Located about 200 meters southeast of the Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun, this double Kofun (also referred to as a {{ill|Rectangular Kofun|ja|長方形墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rectangular Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) measures approximately 60 meters in length and 25 meters in width, with a mound height of about 6–4.8 meters. It is believed to contain two nearly identical horizontal stone chambers. There is a tradition that this is the joint tomb of Empress Suiko and {{ill|Prince Takeda|ja|竹田皇子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Takeda|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11599359}}.
; {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamurozuka Kofun|ja|葉室塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamurozuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 葉室古墳群}}
: A rectangular mound measuring 75 meters east–west and 55 meters north–south, with a mound height of approximately 8 meters. The western portion of the mound is significantly damaged. Surrounding the Hamurozuka Kofun are smaller Kofuns, including:
:* Mondō Kamizuka Kofun (Round mound)
:* {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Kamadozuka Kofun|ja|釜戸塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamadozuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 葉室古墳群}} (Round mound)
:* {{ill|Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamuro Kofun Group|lt=Hamusho Ishizuka Kofun|ja|葉室石塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamusho Ishizuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 葉室古墳群}} (Unknown type)
:* Associated tumuli (smaller mounds connected to larger tombs)
== Notes ==
The name "Okuno Kofun" refers to a Kofun in the Shinagadani area. While some sources identify it as an alternative name for the {{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}}, others associate it with the mausoleum of Prince Shōtoku.<small>Reference: [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/sightseeing/rekishi/rekishi04.html Taishi Town Website]</small> The Isonokami Valley is also home to a tumulus known as "Okushiro Kofun," which is sometimes identified with the {{ill|Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|ja|太子西山古墳|敏達天皇陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishi Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} or with Prince Shōtoku's mausoleum, depending on the source.<small> (Reference: [http://www.town.taishi.osaka.jp/sightseeing/rekishi/rekishi04.html Taishi Town website])</small>
